Every canonical Paper I identity whose proof uses only the operations listed in a realization functor's verified preservation profile remains valid after applying that functor. If the proof uses a domain-specific hypothesis not encoded by the functor, that hypothesis must be verified separately before the transported statement is promoted to a theorem.

A domain theorem is a semantic realization of a canonical seed-calculus theorem only when: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item an explicit realization functor or intertwining construction is given; \item the preservation profile covers every construction used in the canonical proof; \item every additional analytic, finiteness, convergence, positivity, or integrality hypothesis is verified in the domain; \item the resulting conclusion is stated in the domain's native objects. \end{enumerate} Reuse of the words ``seed'', ``packet'', or ``transfer'' without these data is only syntactic reuse.

The later example pass for Paper I is reserved for exactly four canonical realizations: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item a typed quiver reachability model; \item an algebraic coordinate-ring presentation; \item a companion and repeated-primary single-operator model; \item path and cycle adjacency models. \end{enumerate} The bilateral shift belongs to Paper V, while computational orbit-hull and graph-rank algorithms belong to the verification supplement or Paper VIII.
The canonical Paper I export is

expr.tex: \boxed{ \mathsf{PSC}_I= \left( \begin{array}{c} \text{typed grammars and realized operator algebras},\\ \text{seed systems, free presentations, and seed rank},\\ \text{module-top, semisimple, and single-operator formulas},\\ \text{finite and unconditional packet coordinates},\\ \text{transfer blocks and support algebras},\\ \text{reachability and packet-pure source generation},\\ \text{morphisms, invariant exact sequences, quotients, completions},\\ \text{realization functors and equational theorem transport} \end{array} \right). }
